speech_verification.heard: Twenty-nine secret invasion ships sat packed beam-to-beam at Pearl Harbor. High-octane gasoline sat on deck next to mortar ammunition. At 3.08 p.m., a sudden blast ripped through LSD-353. Fires jumped ship to ship, sinking six military vessels. About one-third of the 163 dead were black segregated soldiers. The military quickly classified the tragedy and buried it until 1960. Yet today, only a single rusting bow still sits there.
